units.text: INT. CAR WASH TUNNEL - DAY
A sedan is stuck mid-tunnel between two spinning brushes.
Foam climbs the windows.
FELIX TANAKA-REYES (30s, tie loosened) grips the wheel.
GLORIA PUCKETT (60s, his mother-in-law, handbag on her lap) sits rigid in the passenger seat.
It's fine. The belt does this.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: The belt does what, Felix?
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: Pauses. For the soap to dwell.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Gloria nods slowly.
The brushes whirl.
A wipe of foam slides down the glass.
Felix cracks his window an inch and sniffs it, then closes it again.
You said you'd get the car cleaned before the dinner.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: I am getting the car cleaned before the dinner.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: We're going to be late.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: We're going to be clean.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: A thump from somewhere underneath.
The car shudders.
Gloria opens her handbag, takes out a tissue, and folds it twice.
Felix watches her do it.
He turns off the radio.
Gloria, I want to say something.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: Felix, I want to say something.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: I'm sorry about the wedding toast.
units.name: FELIX

units.text: ^I'm sorry about the wedding toast.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: They look at each other.
The brushes stop.
Foam slides.
Gloria replaces the tissue in her handbag and snaps it shut.
Felix puts both hands on the wheel.
The green light outside does not come on.
